lima.name: Lima
lima.description: Lima is the capital city of Peru, known for its rich cultural heritage, colonial architecture, and delicious food.
lima.history: Founded in 1535, Lima has a fascinating history that includes Spanish colonization and the rise of Peru’s independence.
lima.culture: Lima’s culture blends native, colonial, and modern influences, with vibrant festivals and rich culinary traditions.
lima.weather: Lima has a mild desert climate with temperatures ranging from 17°C to 28°C.

trujillo.name: Trujillo
trujillo.description: Trujillo is known as the 'City of Eternal Spring' and is a northern coastal city full of colonial charm, traditional dance, and archeological wonders.
trujillo.history: Founded in 1534, Trujillo played a significant role in Peru’s independence and is near the ancient pre-Incan city of Chan Chan.
trujillo.culture: Trujillo is famous for the Marinera dance, elegant festivals, and a vibrant mix of colonial and Moche/Chimú heritage.
trujillo.weather: Trujillo has a mild desert climate, with temperatures ranging from 17°C to 25°C and very little rainfall.

ica.name: Ica
ica.description: Ica is a sunny desert city known for its vineyards, sand dunes, and the stunning Huacachina oasis.
ica.history: Once a center of the Paracas and Nazca cultures, Ica later became an important agricultural hub during colonial times.
ica.culture: Ica celebrates grape harvests with pisco festivals and parades, reflecting a rich viticulture and desert lifestyle.
ica.weather: Ica has a hot desert climate, with temperatures between 18°C and 32°C and sunny days almost year-round.

puno.name: Puno
puno.description: Puno is a high-altitude city located on the shores of Lake Titicaca, famous for its indigenous cultures and floating reed islands.
puno.history: Puno was a key region during the rise of the Inca Empire and remains a center of Aymara and Quechua traditions.
puno.culture: Known as Peru’s folkloric capital, Puno hosts colorful festivals like the Virgen de la Candelaria and maintains deep ancestral roots.
puno.weather: Puno has a cold highland climate, with temperatures between 2°C and 16°C and chilly nights throughout the year.

cajamarca.name: Cajamarca
cajamarca.description: Cajamarca is a charming highland city known for its colonial architecture, thermal baths, and historical significance.
cajamarca.history: Cajamarca was the site of the capture of Inca emperor Atahualpa by the Spanish in 1532, marking a pivotal point in Peru’s conquest.
cajamarca.culture: The city hosts one of Peru's most traditional carnivals, blending Andean and Spanish customs in music, dance, and costumes.
cajamarca.weather: Cajamarca has a mild highland climate, with temperatures averaging 6°C to 21°C and frequent sun during the day.

arequipa.name: Arequipa
arequipa.description: Arequipa, known as the 'White City', is famous for its stunning colonial buildings made from white volcanic stone and its nearby volcanoes.
arequipa.history: Founded in 1540, Arequipa was a Spanish stronghold and has a rich republican history, now recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
arequipa.culture: The city blends Spanish influence with local traditions, and its cuisine is among the most diverse and flavorful in Peru.
arequipa.weather: Arequipa has a temperate desert climate, with daytime temperatures between 10°C and 25°C, and lots of sunshine.

cusco.name: Cusco
cusco.description: Cusco is the historic capital of the Inca Empire, full of archaeological ruins, colonial buildings, and pathways to Machu Picchu.
cusco.history: Once the center of Incan civilization, Cusco became a Spanish colonial gem and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
cusco.culture: Cusco celebrates vibrant Andean traditions, colorful festivals, and Quechua heritage, all surrounded by mountain landscapes.
cusco.weather: Cusco has a dry and mild climate, with temperatures from 5°C to 20°C, and colder nights due to the altitude.

iquitos.name: Iquitos
iquitos.description: Iquitos is the largest city in the Peruvian Amazon, accessible only by river or air, and is known for its biodiversity and jungle excursions.
iquitos.history: Founded in the 18th century, Iquitos flourished during the rubber boom and developed a unique culture deep in the Amazon rainforest.
iquitos.culture: The city has a mix of jungle traditions, indigenous culture, and colonial roots, with lively markets and river life.
iquitos.weather: Iquitos has a hot and humid rainforest climate, with temperatures ranging from 23°C to 33°C and frequent rainfall.
